4. //! Kernel frame type.
5. //!
6. //! A [`KernelFrame`] represents a single page-sized physical frame allocated for kernel use.
7. //! It provides `Deref`/`DerefMut` for direct kernel access (identity-mapped) and frees the
8. //! underlying frame on drop via the global frame allocator.
9. 
10. //==================================================================================================
11. // Imports
12. //==================================================================================================
13. 
14. use vstd::prelude::*;
15. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
16. include!("kframe.spec.rs");
17. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
18. include!("kframe.proof.rs");
19. 
20. use crate::hal::mem::{
21.     Address,
22.     FrameAddress,
23.     PageAligned,
24.     PhysicalAddress,
25. };
26. use ::arch::mem;
27. use ::core::ops::{
28.     Deref,
29.     DerefMut,
30. };
31. use ::sys::error::Error;
32. 
33. //==================================================================================================
34. // Kernel Frame
35. //==================================================================================================
36. 
37. /// A type that represents a kernel frame.
38. #[derive(Debug)]
39. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
40. pub struct KernelFrame {
41.     /// Frame address.
42.     base: FrameAddress,
43. }
44. 
45. // Dependency contract for the manager layer: wrapping a `FrameAddress` produces a handle whose
46. // abstract address is the same physical frame.
47. #[verus_verify]
48. impl KernelFrame {
49.     ///
50.     /// # Description
51.     ///
52.     /// Instantiates a kernel frame.
53.     ///
54.     /// # Parameters
55.     ///
56.     /// - `base`: Frame address.
57.     ///
58.     /// # Returns
59.     ///
60.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
61.     ///
62.     // Wrapping a frame produces a handle whose abstract address is the same physical frame
63.     // (`kf@ == base@`) and which is well-formed (`kf.inv()`, page alignment carried from
64.     // `base.inv()`). The identity-mapping side effect is delegated to [`KernelFrame::map_frame`],
65.     // an exec-only helper outside Verus' purview (it materializes a page-table entry through the
66.     // not-yet-verified `mm::virt` layer, whose global `identity_map_view().inv()` precondition
67.     // cannot be discharged from within `mm::phys`). Verus verifies only the pure wrap here.
68.     #[verus_spec(result =>
69.         requires
70.             base.inv(),
71.         ensures
72.             match result {
73.                 Ok(kf) => {
74.                     &&& kf@ == base@
75.                     &&& kf.inv()
76.                 },
77.                 Err(_) => true,
78.             },
79.     )]
80.     pub(super) fn new(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
81.         // Ensure the frame is identity-mapped in the kernel address space so that
82.         // Deref/DerefMut can safely access it. This lazily installs a page
83.         // table entry if needed (page tables come from a BSS pool, so no recursive frame
84.         // allocation occurs).
85.         Self::map_frame(base)?;
86. 
87.         Ok(Self { base })
88.     }
89. }
90. 
91. // Exec-only helper: installs the identity mapping for `base` via `mm::virt::identity_map_page`.
92. // VERUS REWRITE: extracted from the body of `KernelFrame::new` so the pure frame-wrap can be
93. // machine-verified while the cross-module page-table side effect is isolated behind a single,
94. // empty trusted contract (`assume_specification[ KernelFrame::map_frame ]` in kframe.spec.rs,
95. // ledgered in verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md). Inlining the side effect back into the verified
96. // `new` is impossible: (1) `identity_map_page` requires `identity_map_view().inv()`, an
97. // `uninterp spec fn` in the PRIVATE `mod identity_map` that is not re-exported and therefore
98. // cannot even be NAMED from `mm::phys`; (2) `PageAligned::from_raw_value` is external and would
99. // itself need an `assume_specification`; (3) the `error!` logging macros fail to verify
100. // ("Unsupported constant type") and would require cfg-gated exec. Option A thus multiplies
101. // trusted surface and still cannot discharge the precondition; this extraction trusts strictly
102. // less. Kept outside Verus (no `#[verus_verify]`); carries no `external_body`.
103. impl KernelFrame {
104.     fn map_frame(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
105.         let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
106.             PageAligned::from_raw_value(base.into_raw_value()).map_err(|e| {
107.                 error!("frame base is not page-aligned: {e:?}");
108.                 e
109.             })?;
110.         crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page(phys_addr).map_err(|e| {
111.             error!("failed to identity-map frame: {:?}", e);
112.             e
113.         })
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. #[verus_verify]
118. impl KernelFrame {
119. 
120.     ///
121.     /// # Description
122.     ///
123.     /// Returns the base address of the target kernel frame.
124.     ///
125.     /// # Returns
126.     ///
127.     /// The base address of the target kernel frame.
128.     ///
129.     // Pure accessor: returns the owned frame's physical address unchanged. `result@ == self@`
130.     // gives `kpage` the exact address; `result.inv()` (page alignment carried from `self.inv()`)
131.     // lets `into_page_address` and the `KernelStack` arithmetic behind it proceed.
132.     #[verus_spec(result =>
133.         requires
134.             self.inv(),
135.         ensures
136.             result@ == self@,
137.             result.inv(),
138.     )]
139.     pub fn base(&self) -> FrameAddress {
140.         self.base
141.     }
142. }
143. 
144. impl KernelFrame {
145. 
146.     ///
147.     /// # Description
148.     ///
149.     /// Clears the target kernel frame.
150.     ///
151.     /// Uses the identity-map `memset` backend so that the write runs in the kernel address space.
152.     /// This avoids a page fault when the current CR3 points to a user page directory that lacks
153.     /// the PDE for this frame's physical address.
154.     ///
155.     pub fn clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
156.         let base: *mut u8 = self.base.into_raw_value() as *mut u8;
157.         crate::mm::virt::memset(base, 0, mem::PAGE_SIZE).map_err(|e| {
158.             error!("memset failed: {:?}", e);
159.             e
160.         })
161.     }
162. }
163. 
164. /// # Safety
165. ///
166. /// `Deref` accesses the identity-mapped frame directly. The caller must ensure that the current
167. /// CR3 points to a page directory that has the relevant PDE for this frame's physical address
168. /// (i.e., the kernel page directory, or a user page directory into which the PDE has been
169. /// propagated via [`sync_kernel_pdes`](crate::mm::virt::sync_kernel_pdes)). For CR3-agnostic
170. /// writes, prefer [`KernelFrame::clear()`] which uses the identity-map `memset` backend.
171. impl Deref for KernelFrame {
172.     type Target = [u8];
173. 
174.     fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
175.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
176.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr as *const u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
177.     }
178. }
179. 
180. /// # Safety
181. ///
182. /// See [`Deref`] impl — the same CR3 invariant applies.
183. impl DerefMut for KernelFrame {
184.     fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
185.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
186.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(ptr as *mut u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
187.     }
188. }
189. 
190. #[verus_verify]
191. impl Drop for KernelFrame {
192.     // Releasing the handle returns its physical frame to the global frame allocator via
193.     // `super::frame::free`, which is best-effort (`ensures true`) and `opens_invariants none`/
194.     // `no_unwind`, so `drop` makes no abstract postcondition. Callers (the manager error path,
195.     // `KernelStack::drop`) rely on this being the sole, complete deallocation step. Mirror of
196.     // `UserFrame::drop`.
197.     #[verus_spec(
198.         opens_invariants none
199.         no_unwind
200.     )]
201.     fn drop(&mut self) {
202.         if let Err(e) = super::frame::free(self.base) {
203.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
204.             error!("failed to free kernel frame: {:?}", e);
205.         }
206.     }
207. }

# Bugs — `mm::phys::kframe`

No correctness/logic bugs found in the in-scope functions
(`KernelFrame::new`, `KernelFrame::base`, `KernelFrame::drop`).

## Build-hygiene fix (auto-fixed) — duplicate import (kframe.rs)

**What**: `kframe.rs` imported `vstd::prelude::*` twice — `use vstd::prelude::*;`
(top, required so Verus attribute macros parse/erase correctly) and a redundant
`use ::vstd::prelude::*;` lower down.

**Why**: In the normal (non-Verus) `cargo build`, the Verus constructs are erased,
so the glob import is otherwise unused. With two identical glob imports, rustc
flags the second as `unused import`, which is promoted to a hard error under the
crate's `-D warnings`. This broke dual compilation (`./z build -- all-kernel`).
The sibling `mm::phys::upool` has only the single top-of-file import and builds
cleanly.

**Verification Failure**: Not a Verus failure (Verus build passed). Surfaced by
`./z build -- all-kernel`: `error: unused import: ::vstd::prelude::*`.

**How Verus Helped**: The dual-compilation requirement (Verus build + normal
build) exposed a latent redundant import that a Verus-only or normal-only build
in isolation would not necessarily flag the same way.

**Severity**: cosmetic / build-hygiene (no runtime effect).

**Suggested Fix / Auto-Fixed**: Yes — removed the redundant
`use ::vstd::prelude::*;`, keeping the single top-of-file `use vstd::prelude::*;`
(matching `upool.rs`). Both Verus verification and normal build pass afterwards.

## Proving-phase note — `KernelFrame::new` retains sanctioned `external_body`

**What**: The `strip-external-body` proving step removed `#[verus_verify(external_body)]`
from `KernelFrame::new`, which broke compilation (Verus "Unsupported constant type"
on the `error!` macro) and then required a spec for `PageAligned::from_raw_value`.

**Why it must stay `external_body`**: `new`'s body calls
`crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page`, whose precondition is `identity_map_view().inv()`
— a global well-formedness invariant of the **not-yet-verified** `mm::virt` module
(`identity_map_view()` is `uninterp`; its `inv()` is not a tautology and `mm::virt`
itself still carries `admit()`). This precondition cannot be discharged within
`mm::phys` without (a) `admit()` (forbidden), (b) adding a `requires` to `new`
(spec weakening — restricts the manager callers, forbidden), or (c) touching the
out-of-scope `mm::virt` layer. `new` is explicitly listed in `tcb-allowed.md`
("Cross-module dependencies marked external_body"), so `external_body` is the sound,
rule-compliant choice until `mm::virt` is verified, at which point the trusted bridge
for `identity_map_view().inv()` (mirroring `frame::instance()` pinning `phys_view()`)
becomes available and the `external_body` can be eliminated.

**Resolution**: Restored `external_body` on `new` (matching the spec-phase design and
the prior known-good PASS). `KernelFrame::base` and `KernelFrame::drop` are fully
verified in-body (0 `admit`, 0 `assume`). Not a code bug.

`./z build -- all-kernel`: `error: unused import: ::vstd::prelude::*`.

**How Verus Helped**: The dual-compilation requirement (Verus build + normal
build) exposed a latent redundant import that a Verus-only or normal-only build
in isolation would not necessarily flag the same way.

**Severity**: cosmetic / build-hygiene (no runtime effect).

**Suggested Fix / Auto-Fixed**: Yes — removed the redundant
`use ::vstd::prelude::*;`, keeping the single top-of-file `use vstd::prelude::*;`
(matching `upool.rs`). Both Verus verification and normal build pass afterwards.

## Proving-phase note — `KernelFrame::new` retains sanctioned `external_body`

**What**: The `strip-external-body` proving step removed `#[verus_verify(external_body)]`
from `KernelFrame::new`, which broke compilation (Verus "Unsupported constant type"
on the `error!` macro) and then required a spec for `PageAligned::from_raw_value`.

**Why it must stay `external_body`**: `new`'s body calls
`crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page`, whose precondition is `identity_map_view().inv()`
— a global well-formedness invariant of the **not-yet-verified** `mm::virt` module
(`identity_map_view()` is `uninterp`; its `inv()` is not a tautology and `mm::virt`
itself still carries `admit()`). This precondition cannot be discharged within
`mm::phys` without (a) `admit()` (forbidden), (b) adding a `requires` to `new`
(spec weakening — restricts the manager callers, forbidden), or (c) touching the
out-of-scope `mm::virt` layer. `new` is explicitly listed in `tcb-allowed.md`
("Cross-module dependencies marked external_body"), so `external_body` is the sound,
rule-compliant choice until `mm::virt` is verified, at which point the trusted bridge
for `identity_map_view().inv()` (mirroring `frame::instance()` pinning `phys_view()`)
becomes available and the `external_body` can be eliminated.

**Resolution**: Restored `external_body` on `new` (matching the spec-phase design and
the prior known-good PASS). `KernelFrame::base` and `KernelFrame::drop` are fully
verified in-body (0 `admit`, 0 `assume`). Not a code bug.

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs:464` — `alloc_many_kernel_frames`:
  ```rust
  match FrameAddress::from_raw_value(raw_addr).and_then(KernelFrame::new) {
      Ok(kf) => frames.push(kf),
      Err(e) => { frames.clear(); /* free remaining raw frames */ }
  }
  ```
  Addresses come from a contiguous allocation `frame::alloc_contiguous(count)`.
  Each `raw_addr` is page-aligned by construction. The spec requires that the
  pushed handle's view equals the contiguous physical address
  (`kernel_frames_contiguous`, `kernel_addr_set(final(frames)@)`), again relying
  on `kf@ == base@`.

### `KernelFrame::drop` — trait `Drop`, implicit (compiler-dispatched)
No explicit call sites; runs when a `KernelFrame` goes out of scope. Implicit
drop sites observed:

- `mm::phys::manager::alloc_many_kernel_frames` error path: `frames.clear()`
  drops already-wrapped `KernelFrame`s, "frees them via `KernelFrame::Drop`"
  (comment at `manager.rs:467`).
- `mm::kstack::KernelStack::drop` (`kstack.rs:334`) pops and drops `KernelPage`s,
  each of which owns a `KernelFrame`, transitively dropping it.
- Any `KernelFrame`/`KernelPage`/`KernelStack` value that goes out of scope.

The drop body calls `super::frame::free(self.base)` — i.e. dropping a handle
returns its physical frame to the global allocator.

### `KernelFrame::base` — `pub`, 2 call sites
Both in `mm::virt::kpage`:

- `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/kpage.rs:58` — `KernelPage::base`:
  `self.kframe.base().into_page_address().into_virtual_address()`.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/kpage.rs:74` — `KernelPage::frame_address`:
  returns `self.kframe.base()` directly.

Both callers treat `base()` as a pure accessor that yields the frame's
`FrameAddress`, then convert it to page/virtual addresses. They rely on the
returned value being exactly the address the frame was created with (and being
page-aligned, since `into_page_address` and `KernelStack` arithmetic assume it).

---

## Trait Obligations
- Trait `Drop` (`KernelFrame::drop`) — expected semantics: releasing the handle
  returns ownership of the underlying physical frame to the global frame
  allocator exactly once (`super::frame::free(self.base)`). Callers
  (`alloc_many_kernel_frames` error path, `KernelStack::drop`) depend on drop
  being the *sole* and *complete* deallocation step — they do not free the frame
  themselves once it has been wrapped in a `KernelFrame`.
- Traits `Deref` / `DerefMut` — out of scope here; provide identity-mapped slice
  access (CR3 invariant documented in source).

---

## Caller Expectations

### `KernelFrame::new`
- Callers assume: on `Ok(kf)`, the handle owns the *same* physical frame that was
  passed in — `kf@ == base@`. The input `base` is always a valid, page-aligned
  address obtained from a successful `frame::alloc()` / `alloc_contiguous()`
  (i.e. `base.inv()` holds).
- Callers assume: on `Err(_)`, `new` did **not** take ownership / did not free the
  frame — the caller is responsible for freeing `base` (it does so explicitly).
  No state guarantee beyond "the wrap failed".
- Callers don't care about: the identity-mapping side effect
  (`mm::virt::identity_map_page`), how page tables are installed, or any internal
  representation beyond the abstract address.

### `KernelFrame::drop`
- Callers assume: dropping frees the underlying physical frame exactly once via
  the global allocator, with no further action required from them.
- Callers don't care about: error handling inside drop (a failed free is only
  logged), or the mechanics of `frame::free`.

### `KernelFrame::base`
- Callers assume: `base()` is a pure, side-effect-free accessor returning the
  frame's `FrameAddress`, equal to the construction address (`result@ == self@`),
  and page-aligned so downstream page/virtual-address conversions are valid.
- Callers don't care about: how `base` is stored internally (field vs. computed).

---

## Abstract Resource
`KernelFrame` is an **owning handle to a single page-sized physical frame** that
is identity-mapped for kernel access. The module manages the ownership lifecycle
of one physical frame: `new` wraps a freshly allocated frame address into an
owning handle, `base` exposes that frame's physical address, and `drop` returns
the frame to the global frame allocator. Its `View` is the physical address
(`int`) of the owned frame.

## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
- A `KernelFrame`'s abstract view is its physical frame address and never
  changes for the lifetime of the handle: `self@ == base@` from construction,
  and `base()` reports the same value.
- `new` preserves the input address on success (`kf@ == base@`) and does not
  consume the frame on failure.
- Each physical frame is owned by at most one live `KernelFrame`; dropping the
  handle frees that frame exactly once. Callers never double-free a wrapped frame.
- `base()` is pure: it does not mutate the handle or the allocator and returns a
  page-aligned `FrameAddress`.

---

## Pre-existing Specs (from upstream verification)
- Source: added during top-down verification of the `mm::phys` manager layer
  (`alloc_kernel_frame`, `alloc_many_kernel_frames`).
- `kframe.spec.rs` and `kframe.proof.rs` are empty (`verus! { }`); the specs live
  inline in `kframe.rs`.
- View type: **exists** — `impl View for KernelFrame { type V = int; view == self.base@ }`
  (closed spec).
- Functions with specs:
  - `KernelFrame::new` — `requires base.inv(); ensures Ok(kf) => kf@ == base@, Err(_) => true`.
    Marked `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` (dependency contract: relies on
    `mm::virt::identity_map_page`, outside `mm::phys` scope).
- Functions WITHOUT specs (in scope):
  - `KernelFrame::base` — no `#[verus_spec]`; needs `ensures result@ == self@`
    (pure accessor) for the `kpage` callers.
  - `KernelFrame::drop` — no `#[verus_spec]`; the manager error-path and
    `KernelStack::drop` rely on it freeing the frame, but its effect on the
    global allocator is not yet captured by a spec.

### Assessment
- Coverage: **partial** — only `new` is specified (what the manager needed for
  `lemma_kernel_alloc_one`). `base` and `drop` are unspecified.
- Strength: **adequate for `new`'s success path** (`kf@ == base@`), but the
  `Err(_) => true` ensures is weak; callers actually rely on the implicit
  contract that `new` does not free/consume the frame on failure (currently
  guaranteed only by `external_body` + manual free at the call site).
- View design: **caller-abstract** — `type V = int` (physical address) matches
  exactly what every caller uses (`kf@`, address comparisons, `kernel_addr_set`,
  `into_page_address`). It does not leak internal representation, so it is a good,
  stable abstraction.

### Recommendations for View/spec design
- Keep `View::V = int` (the physical frame address) — all callers agree on this.
- Add a spec to `base`: `ensures result@ == self@` (pure accessor) so `kpage`
  conversions verify.
- Consider a spec for `drop` capturing the "frees the frame once" effect, so the
  manager error-path and stack teardown can reason about allocator state.

4. //! Kernel frame type.
5. //!
6. //! A [`KernelFrame`] represents a single page-sized physical frame allocated for kernel use.
7. //! It provides `Deref`/`DerefMut` for direct kernel access (identity-mapped) and frees the
8. //! underlying frame on drop via the global frame allocator.
9. 
10. //==================================================================================================
11. // Imports
12. //==================================================================================================
13. 
14. use vstd::prelude::*;
15. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
16. include!("kframe.spec.rs");
17. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
18. include!("kframe.proof.rs");
19. 
20. use crate::hal::mem::{
21.     Address,
22.     FrameAddress,
23.     PageAligned,
24.     PhysicalAddress,
25. };
26. use ::arch::mem;
27. use ::core::ops::{
28.     Deref,
29.     DerefMut,
30. };
31. use ::sys::error::Error;
32. 
33. //==================================================================================================
34. // Kernel Frame
35. //==================================================================================================
36. 
37. /// A type that represents a kernel frame.
38. #[derive(Debug)]
39. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
40. pub struct KernelFrame {
41.     /// Frame address.
42.     base: FrameAddress,
43. }
44. 
45. // Dependency contract for the manager layer: wrapping a `FrameAddress` produces a handle whose
46. // abstract address is the same physical frame.
47. #[verus_verify]
48. impl KernelFrame {
49.     ///
50.     /// # Description
51.     ///
52.     /// Instantiates a kernel frame.
53.     ///
54.     /// # Parameters
55.     ///
56.     /// - `base`: Frame address.
57.     ///
58.     /// # Returns
59.     ///
60.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
61.     ///
62.     // Wrapping a frame produces a handle whose abstract address is the same physical frame
63.     // (`kf@ == base@`) and which is well-formed (`kf.inv()`, page alignment carried from
64.     // `base.inv()`). The identity-mapping side effect is delegated to [`KernelFrame::map_frame`],
65.     // an exec-only helper outside Verus' purview (it materializes a page-table entry through the
66.     // not-yet-verified `mm::virt` layer, whose global `identity_map_view().inv()` precondition
67.     // cannot be discharged from within `mm::phys`). Verus verifies only the pure wrap here.
68.     #[verus_spec(result =>
69.         requires
70.             base.inv(),
71.         ensures
72.             match result {
73.                 Ok(kf) => {
74.                     &&& kf@ == base@
75.                     &&& kf.inv()
76.                 },
77.                 Err(_) => true,
78.             },
79.     )]
80.     pub(super) fn new(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
81.         // Ensure the frame is identity-mapped in the kernel address space so that
82.         // Deref/DerefMut can safely access it. This lazily installs a page
83.         // table entry if needed (page tables come from a BSS pool, so no recursive frame
84.         // allocation occurs).
85.         Self::map_frame(base)?;
86. 
87.         Ok(Self { base })
88.     }
89. }
90. 
91. // Exec-only helper: installs the identity mapping for `base` via `mm::virt::identity_map_page`.
92. // VERUS REWRITE: extracted from the body of `KernelFrame::new` so the pure frame-wrap can be
93. // machine-verified while the cross-module page-table side effect is isolated behind a single,
94. // empty trusted contract (`assume_specification[ KernelFrame::map_frame ]` in kframe.spec.rs,
95. // ledgered in verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md). Inlining the side effect back into the verified
96. // `new` is impossible: (1) `identity_map_page` requires `identity_map_view().inv()`, an
97. // `uninterp spec fn` in the PRIVATE `mod identity_map` that is not re-exported and therefore
98. // cannot even be NAMED from `mm::phys`; (2) `PageAligned::from_raw_value` is external and would
99. // itself need an `assume_specification`; (3) the `error!` logging macros fail to verify
100. // ("Unsupported constant type") and would require cfg-gated exec. Option A thus multiplies
101. // trusted surface and still cannot discharge the precondition; this extraction trusts strictly
102. // less. Kept outside Verus (no `#[verus_verify]`); carries no `external_body`.
103. impl KernelFrame {
104.     fn map_frame(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
105.         let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
106.             PageAligned::from_raw_value(base.into_raw_value()).map_err(|e| {
107.                 error!("frame base is not page-aligned: {e:?}");
108.                 e
109.             })?;
110.         crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page(phys_addr).map_err(|e| {
111.             error!("failed to identity-map frame: {:?}", e);
112.             e
113.         })
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. #[verus_verify]
118. impl KernelFrame {
119. 
120.     ///
121.     /// # Description
122.     ///
123.     /// Returns the base address of the target kernel frame.
124.     ///
125.     /// # Returns
126.     ///
127.     /// The base address of the target kernel frame.
128.     ///
129.     // Pure accessor: returns the owned frame's physical address unchanged. `result@ == self@`
130.     // gives `kpage` the exact address; `result.inv()` (page alignment carried from `self.inv()`)
131.     // lets `into_page_address` and the `KernelStack` arithmetic behind it proceed.
132.     #[verus_spec(result =>
133.         requires
134.             self.inv(),
135.         ensures
136.             result@ == self@,
137.             result.inv(),
138.     )]
139.     pub fn base(&self) -> FrameAddress {
140.         self.base
141.     }
142. }
143. 
144. impl KernelFrame {
145. 
146.     ///
147.     /// # Description
148.     ///
149.     /// Clears the target kernel frame.
150.     ///
151.     /// Uses the identity-map `memset` backend so that the write runs in the kernel address space.
152.     /// This avoids a page fault when the current CR3 points to a user page directory that lacks
153.     /// the PDE for this frame's physical address.
154.     ///
155.     pub fn clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
156.         let base: *mut u8 = self.base.into_raw_value() as *mut u8;
157.         crate::mm::virt::memset(base, 0, mem::PAGE_SIZE).map_err(|e| {
158.             error!("memset failed: {:?}", e);
159.             e
160.         })
161.     }
162. }
163. 
164. /// # Safety
165. ///
166. /// `Deref` accesses the identity-mapped frame directly. The caller must ensure that the current
167. /// CR3 points to a page directory that has the relevant PDE for this frame's physical address
168. /// (i.e., the kernel page directory, or a user page directory into which the PDE has been
169. /// propagated via [`sync_kernel_pdes`](crate::mm::virt::sync_kernel_pdes)). For CR3-agnostic
170. /// writes, prefer [`KernelFrame::clear()`] which uses the identity-map `memset` backend.
171. impl Deref for KernelFrame {
172.     type Target = [u8];
173. 
174.     fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
175.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
176.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr as *const u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
177.     }
178. }
179. 
180. /// # Safety
181. ///
182. /// See [`Deref`] impl — the same CR3 invariant applies.
183. impl DerefMut for KernelFrame {
184.     fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
185.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
186.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(ptr as *mut u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
187.     }
188. }
189. 
190. #[verus_verify]
191. impl Drop for KernelFrame {
192.     // Releasing the handle returns its physical frame to the global frame allocator via
193.     // `super::frame::free`, which is best-effort (`ensures true`) and `opens_invariants none`/
194.     // `no_unwind`, so `drop` makes no abstract postcondition. Callers (the manager error path,
195.     // `KernelStack::drop`) rely on this being the sole, complete deallocation step. Mirror of
196.     // `UserFrame::drop`.
197.     #[verus_spec(
198.         opens_invariants none
199.         no_unwind
200.     )]
201.     fn drop(&mut self) {
202.         if let Err(e) = super::frame::free(self.base) {
203.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
204.             error!("failed to free kernel frame: {:?}", e);
205.         }
206.     }
207. }

1. # View Design: `mm::phys::kframe` (`KernelFrame`)
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. `KernelFrame` is an **owning handle to exactly one page-sized physical frame**.
6. To the outside world it is a single value: *which physical frame this handle
7. owns*. The only caller-observable abstract state is that frame's **physical
8. address**. Everything else — the identity-mapping side effect, how the address
9. is stored, the page-table mechanics, the byte contents reachable through
10. `Deref` — is internal or out of scope.
11. 
12. In-scope functions: `KernelFrame::new` (constructor), `KernelFrame::base`
13. (query), `KernelFrame::drop` (destructor).
14. 
15. ---
16. 
17. ## Inherited View (from upstream `mm::phys` manager verification)
18. 
19. ```rust
20. impl View for KernelFrame {
21.     type V = int;
22.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int { self.base@ }   // physical frame address
23. }
24. ```
25. 
26. This View was added when the manager layer (`alloc_kernel_frame`,
27. `alloc_many_kernel_frames`) was verified top-down. It is treated here as an
28. **input to evaluate**, not a finished design.
29. 
30. ### Evaluation against *all* callers
31. 
32. | Caller | Uses `self@` as… | Verdict |
33. |---|---|---|
34. | `manager::alloc_kernel_frame` | the allocated address: `kf@ == frame_addr@`, `lemma_kernel_alloc_one(..., result->Ok_0@)` | ✅ address |
35. | `manager::alloc_many_kernel_frames` | `kernel_frames_contiguous`, `kernel_addr_set(frames@)` — set/sequence of owned addresses | ✅ address |
36. | `virt::kpage::KernelPage::base` | `kframe.base().into_page_address().into_virtual_address()` — needs the address + page-alignment | ✅ address |
37. | `virt::kpage::KernelPage::frame_address` | returns `kframe.base()` verbatim | ✅ address |
38. | `Drop` sites (manager error path, `KernelStack::drop`) | identity of the frame being freed exactly once | ✅ address |
39. 
40. Every caller agrees: the abstract state is the **physical frame address**, an
41. `int`. No caller needs anything else.
42. 
43. **Decision: KEEP `type V = int` unchanged.** It already passes the
44. substitution test from every caller's perspective (see Rationale). Nothing is
45. renamed, added, or removed. The View definition is left exactly as inherited.
46. 
47. ---
48. 
49. ## View Struct
50. 
51. The View is a primitive, not a struct:
52. 
53. ```rust
54. impl View for KernelFrame {
55.     type V = int;                       // the physical address of the owned frame
56.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int { /* maps impl field -> address */ }
57. }
58. ```
59. 
60. - `view()` stays **`closed`**: public so callers write `kf@`, closed so the
61.   field-level mapping (currently `self.base@`) does not leak.
62. - The value space is `int` — the mathematical physical address. (Per the
63.   view-design exception, an address could keep `usize`; here the upstream View
64.   and the whole `FrameAddress`/`Inner` address algebra already work in `int`
65.   via `View::V = int`, so `int` is the consistent, cast-free choice.)
66. 
67. A wrapper struct (`KernelFrameView { addr: int }`) was considered and
68. **rejected** — see Rejected Alternatives.
69. 
70. ---
71. 
72. ## Well-formedness Invariant
73. 
74. `KernelFrame` currently has **no** `inv()`. Callers of `base()`
75. (`into_page_address`, and the page/stack address arithmetic behind it) rely on
76. the owned address being **page-aligned**. This is a caller-visible constraint
77. on the abstract state, so it belongs in `inv()`.
78. 
79. **Final decision (spec phase): single `inv()`, mirroring the verified sibling
80. `UserFrame::inv`.** The originally-sketched `internal_inv()` placeholder
81. (`pub closed spec fn internal_inv(&self) -> bool { true }`) was dropped: it would
82. be permanently `true` (the closed view `self@ == self.base@` already exposes the
83. alignment fact directly, so no implementation-consistency clause is needed), and
84. the `spec-design` skill discourages extra `pub spec fn`s on `impl MyType` beyond
85. `view`/`inv`. The result is identical in shape to `UserFrame`:
86. 
87. ```rust
88. impl KernelFrame {
89.     // Caller-visible well-formedness: the owned frame address is page-aligned.
90.     // Stated purely on the int view via the shared spec_page_size(); leaks no
91.     // implementation detail. Mirror of UserFrame::inv.
92.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
93.         self@ % spec_page_size() == 0
94.     }
95. }
96. ```
97. 
98. - `inv()` is **`pub open`** so callers can establish and consume it.
99. - `spec_page_size()` is the same `pub uninterp spec fn` already used by
100.   `FrameAddress::inv` (`self@ % spec_page_size() == 0`); reusing it keeps the
101.   alignment notion identical across the two types.
102. - No `internal_inv()` is defined; the alignment fact follows on the `new` /
103.   `base` paths directly from the required `base.inv()` / `self.inv()`.
104. 
105. No other `pub spec fn` is added to `impl KernelFrame` beyond `view` and `inv`.
106. 
107. ---
108. 
109. ## Spec Transition Functions
110. 
111. **There are none — and that is a deliberate, substitution-tested result.**
112. 
113. A `KernelFrame`'s abstract view is fixed at construction and **never changes**
114. for the lifetime of the handle. The in-scope API confirms this:
115. 
116. - `new(base)` is a **constructor**: it produces a fresh handle whose view *is*
117.   the input address. The contract is a constructor postcondition, not a
118.   transition on an existing view:
119. 
120.   ```rust
121.   // new (already external_body per tcb-allowed.md; keep its existing spec,
122.   // optionally surface the invariant it already guarantees):
123.   ensures match result {
124.       Ok(kf) => kf@ == base@ && kf.inv(),   // inv follows from required base.inv()
125.       Err(_) => true,                       // no ownership taken on failure
126.   }
127.   ```
128. 
129. - `base(&self)` is a **pure query** — no view change. Needed new spec:
130. 
131.   ```rust
132.   fn base(&self) -> (result: FrameAddress)
133.       requires self.inv(),
134.       ensures  result@ == self@ && result.inv();
135.   ```
136. 
137.   `result@ == self@` gives `kpage` the exact address; `result.inv()` (carried
138.   from `self.inv()`'s alignment clause) lets `into_page_address` and the stack
139.   arithmetic proceed.
140. 
141. - `drop(&mut self)` is a **destructor**. Its effect is *not* a transition on
142.   `KernelFrame`'s own view (the value is consumed). Dropping returns the frame
143.   `old(self)@` to the **global frame allocator**, so its postcondition is
144.   written against the allocator's View (`FrameAllocView` / `phys_view().frames`,
145.   the same View the manager already reasons over), e.g. "after drop,
146.   `old(self)@` is no longer allocated / is back in the free partition, and no
147.   other frame's status changes." Because that state lives in the allocator's
148.   abstraction, **no field is needed on `KernelFrameView` to express it**.
149. 
150. Consequently `impl KernelFrame`'s View needs no `spec_*` mutator helpers: the
151. view is immutable per handle, the only state change in the module
152. (allocation/free) is owned by the allocator's View.
153. 
154. ---
155. 
156. ## Design Rationale
157. 
158. ### Field: the view value `self@ : int` — the physical frame address
159. - **Why needed.** It is the one thing every caller reasons about: the manager
160.   proves the wrapped address equals the allocated address and builds
161.   `kernel_addr_set` / contiguity facts from it; `kpage` converts it to page and
162.   virtual addresses; `drop` frees *that* address. There is no caller use of
163.   `KernelFrame` that does not reduce to its address.
164. - **Substitution test.** *If `KernelFrame` were rewritten to store a raw

 # View Design: `mm::phys::kframe` (`KernelFrame`)
 
 ## Abstract Resource
 
 `KernelFrame` is an **owning handle to exactly one page-sized physical frame**.
 To the outside world it is a single value: *which physical frame this handle
 owns*. The only caller-observable abstract state is that frame's **physical
 address**. Everything else — the identity-mapping side effect, how the address
 is stored, the page-table mechanics, the byte contents reachable through
 `Deref` — is internal or out of scope.
 
 In-scope functions: `KernelFrame::new` (constructor), `KernelFrame::base`
 (query), `KernelFrame::drop` (destructor).
 
 ---
 
 ## Inherited View (from upstream `mm::phys` manager verification)
 
 ```rust
 impl View for KernelFrame {
     type V = int;
     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int { self.base@ }   // physical frame address
 }
 ```
 
 This View was added when the manager layer (`alloc_kernel_frame`,
 `alloc_many_kernel_frames`) was verified top-down. It is treated here as an
 **input to evaluate**, not a finished design.
 
 ### Evaluation against *all* callers
 
 | Caller | Uses `self@` as… | Verdict |
 |---|---|---|
 | `manager::alloc_kernel_frame` | the allocated address: `kf@ == frame_addr@`, `lemma_kernel_alloc_one(..., result->Ok_0@)` | ✅ address |
 | `manager::alloc_many_kernel_frames` | `kernel_frames_contiguous`, `kernel_addr_set(frames@)` — set/sequence of owned addresses | ✅ address |
 | `virt::kpage::KernelPage::base` | `kframe.base().into_page_address().into_virtual_address()` — needs the address + page-alignment | ✅ address |
 | `virt::kpage::KernelPage::frame_address` | returns `kframe.base()` verbatim | ✅ address |
 | `Drop` sites (manager error path, `KernelStack::drop`) | identity of the frame being freed exactly once | ✅ address |
 
 Every caller agrees: the abstract state is the **physical frame address**, an
 `int`. No caller needs anything else.
 
 **Decision: KEEP `type V = int` unchanged.** It already passes the
 substitution test from every caller's perspective (see Rationale). Nothing is
 renamed, added, or removed. The View definition is left exactly as inherited.
 
 ---
 
 ## View Struct
 
 The View is a primitive, not a struct:
 
 ```rust
 impl View for KernelFrame {
     type V = int;                       // the physical address of the owned frame
     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int { /* maps impl field -> address */ }
 }
 ```
 
 - `view()` stays **`closed`**: public so callers write `kf@`, closed so the
   field-level mapping (currently `self.base@`) does not leak.
 - The value space is `int` — the mathematical physical address. (Per the
   view-design exception, an address could keep `usize`; here the upstream View
   and the whole `FrameAddress`/`Inner` address algebra already work in `int`
   via `View::V = int`, so `int` is the consistent, cast-free choice.)
 
 A wrapper struct (`KernelFrameView { addr: int }`) was considered and
 **rejected** — see Rejected Alternatives.
 
 ---
 
 ## Well-formedness Invariant
 
 `KernelFrame` currently has **no** `inv()`. Callers of `base()`
 (`into_page_address`, and the page/stack address arithmetic behind it) rely on
 the owned address being **page-aligned**. This is a caller-visible constraint
 on the abstract state, so it belongs in `inv()`.
 
 **Final decision (spec phase): single `inv()`, mirroring the verified sibling
 `UserFrame::inv`.** The originally-sketched `internal_inv()` placeholder
 (`pub closed spec fn internal_inv(&self) -> bool { true }`) was dropped: it would
 be permanently `true` (the closed view `self@ == self.base@` already exposes the
 alignment fact directly, so no implementation-consistency clause is needed), and
 the `spec-design` skill discourages extra `pub spec fn`s on `impl MyType` beyond
 `view`/`inv`. The result is identical in shape to `UserFrame`:
 
 ```rust
 impl KernelFrame {
     // Caller-visible well-formedness: the owned frame address is page-aligned.
     // Stated purely on the int view via the shared spec_page_size(); leaks no
     // implementation detail. Mirror of UserFrame::inv.
     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
         self@ % spec_page_size() == 0
     }
 }
 ```
 
 - `inv()` is **`pub open`** so callers can establish and consume it.
 - `spec_page_size()` is the same `pub uninterp spec fn` already used by
   `FrameAddress::inv` (`self@ % spec_page_size() == 0`); reusing it keeps the
   alignment notion identical across the two types.
 - No `internal_inv()` is defined; the alignment fact follows on the `new` /
   `base` paths directly from the required `base.inv()` / `self.inv()`.
 
 No other `pub spec fn` is added to `impl KernelFrame` beyond `view` and `inv`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Spec Transition Functions
 
 **There are none — and that is a deliberate, substitution-tested result.**
 
 A `KernelFrame`'s abstract view is fixed at construction and **never changes**
 for the lifetime of the handle. The in-scope API confirms this:
 
 - `new(base)` is a **constructor**: it produces a fresh handle whose view *is*
   the input address. The contract is a constructor postcondition, not a
   transition on an existing view:
 
   ```rust
   // new (already external_body per tcb-allowed.md; keep its existing spec,
   // optionally surface the invariant it already guarantees):
   ensures match result {
       Ok(kf) => kf@ == base@ && kf.inv(),   // inv follows from required base.inv()
       Err(_) => true,                       // no ownership taken on failure
   }
   ```
 
 - `base(&self)` is a **pure query** — no view change. Needed new spec:
 
   ```rust
   fn base(&self) -> (result: FrameAddress)
       requires self.inv(),
       ensures  result@ == self@ && result.inv();
   ```
 
   `result@ == self@` gives `kpage` the exact address; `result.inv()` (carried
   from `self.inv()`'s alignment clause) lets `into_page_address` and the stack
   arithmetic proceed.
 
 - `drop(&mut self)` is a **destructor**. Its effect is *not* a transition on
   `KernelFrame`'s own view (the value is consumed). Dropping returns the frame
   `old(self)@` to the **global frame allocator**, so its postcondition is
   written against the allocator's View (`FrameAllocView` / `phys_view().frames`,
   the same View the manager already reasons over), e.g. "after drop,
   `old(self)@` is no longer allocated / is back in the free partition, and no
   other frame's status changes." Because that state lives in the allocator's
   abstraction, **no field is needed on `KernelFrameView` to express it**.
 
 Consequently `impl KernelFrame`'s View needs no `spec_*` mutator helpers: the
 view is immutable per handle, the only state change in the module
 (allocation/free) is owned by the allocator's View.
 
 ---
 
 ## Design Rationale
 
 ### Field: the view value `self@ : int` — the physical frame address
 - **Why needed.** It is the one thing every caller reasons about: the manager
   proves the wrapped address equals the allocated address and builds
   `kernel_addr_set` / contiguity facts from it; `kpage` converts it to page and
   virtual addresses; `drop` frees *that* address. There is no caller use of
   `KernelFrame` that does not reduce to its address.
 - **Substitution test.** *If `KernelFrame` were rewritten to store a raw
   `usize`, a frame number, or to compute the address on the fly instead of
   holding a `FrameAddress` — would "the physical frame address" still make
   sense?* **Yes.** Any owning-frame-handle implementation must denote *some*
   physical frame; its address is the implementation-independent identity of
   what is owned. ✅
 - **Caller-only.** A caller understands "the physical address of the frame this
   handle owns" with zero knowledge of the internal field, the identity map, or
   page tables.
 
 ### `inv()` clause: `self@ % spec_page_size() == 0` (page-aligned)
 - **Why needed.** `base()` returns a `FrameAddress` that downstream code feeds
   to `into_page_address` and to `KernelStack` index arithmetic, both of which
   assume page alignment. Collecting this into `inv()` (instead of re-deriving it
   at every call site) follows the "missing wf()" anti-pattern fix.
 - **Substitution test.** Alignment is a property of *what a physical frame is*
   (page-sized, page-aligned), not of how the handle stores it. Any
   implementation that owns a real frame yields a page-aligned address. ✅
 - **Caller-abstract.** Stated purely on `self@` using the shared
   `spec_page_size()`; no implementation detail appears.
 
 ### `internal_inv()` left as `true`
 - Per methodology, implementation-consistency facts (here: "the stored
   `FrameAddress` satisfies its own `inv`") require seeing impl fields, so they
   are deferred to the spec phase. The caller-visible consequence (alignment) is
   already exposed through `inv()`.
 
 ### Why no spec transition functions
 - The handle's view is immutable; the only mutation in the module's lifecycle
   (a frame leaving the free partition on `new`'s upstream `alloc`, and returning
   on `drop`) is state of the **allocator**, captured by `FrameAllocView`, not by
   this per-object View. Modeling it here would duplicate (and risk
   desynchronizing) the allocator's abstraction.
 
 ---
 
 ## Rejected Alternatives
 
 1. **Wrapper struct `KernelFrameView { addr: int }`.**
    Rejected for minimality. A one-field struct adds a layer of `.addr`
    projections to every caller spec (`kf@.addr` vs `kf@`) and a `view()` that
    constructs the struct, with zero added information. `type V = int` is the
    simpler, already-adopted, caller-agreed abstraction. The `inv()` predicate
    lives perfectly well on `impl KernelFrame`.
 
 2. **Add an `allocated: bool` / ownership flag, or an allocator reference, to
    the View.**
    Rejected as an abstraction leak / wrong owner. Whether a frame is allocated
    is global allocator state, already modeled by `FrameAllocView`
    (`phys_view().frames`). The manager error path and `KernelStack::drop` reason
    about "freed exactly once" through the allocator's view, not through a flag
    on the handle. Duplicating it here would create two sources of truth that
    must be kept in sync. `drop`'s contract is therefore written against the
    allocator's View, leaving `KernelFrame`'s View minimal.
 
 3. **Add a `mapped: bool` (identity-mapping) field.**
    Rejected. The caller analysis is explicit: callers *do not care* about the
    identity-mapping side effect of `new`. It is an internal effect of
    `mm::virt::identity_map_page` (outside `mm::phys` scope) and observable to no
    in-scope caller. Including it would leak HOW the handle is set up.
 
 4. **Add the frame's byte contents (e.g. `Seq<u8>` / a `PointsTo`) to the
    View.**
    Rejected for this scope. Byte contents are only relevant to `Deref`,
    `DerefMut`, and `clear` — all explicitly **out of scope** and not to be
    touched. The in-scope functions (`new`, `base`, `drop`) concern only frame
    *ownership/identity*, i.e. the address. If/when the access functions are
    verified, the natural model for their bytes is a `PointsTo` over the
    identity-mapped region (keyed by `self@`), not a field baked into this
    ownership View — so adding it now would be premature and would destabilize
    the View the current callers already depend on.
 
 5. **Change `view()` to `usize` instead of `int`.**
    Rejected for consistency. The entire surrounding address algebra
    (`FrameAddress`, `Inner`, `FrameAllocView`, the manager's
    `kernel_addr_set`/contiguity lemmas) is expressed with `View::V = int`.
    Switching this one View to `usize` would force casts at every interface with
    those specs for no benefit; the inherited `int` view is correct as-is.
 
 6. **Strengthen `new`'s `Err(_) => true` into an explicit "frame not consumed"
    postcondition.**
    Considered (the caller does rely on `new` not freeing `base` on failure), but
    **out of scope for View design** and partly outside this module: the
    no-consume guarantee on the error path is currently provided by `new` being a
    trusted `external_body` dependency contract (it never touches the global
    allocator on `Err`) plus the caller's explicit `frame::free(base)` cleanup.
    The View needs no field to express it. Noted here for the spec phase; the
    View design is unaffected.
 
 ---
 
 ## Quality Review
 
 | Criterion | Check |
 |---|---|
 | **Substitution** | The address (and its page-alignment) survive any rewrite of how the handle stores/derives the frame. ✅ |
 | **Caller-only** | Every caller reads `kf@` as "the owned frame's physical address" with no impl knowledge. ✅ |

4. //! Kernel frame type.
5. //!
6. //! A [`KernelFrame`] represents a single page-sized physical frame allocated for kernel use.
7. //! It provides `Deref`/`DerefMut` for direct kernel access (identity-mapped) and frees the
8. //! underlying frame on drop via the global frame allocator.
9. 
10. //==================================================================================================
11. // Imports
12. //==================================================================================================
13. 
14. use vstd::prelude::*;
15. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
16. include!("kframe.spec.rs");
17. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
18. include!("kframe.proof.rs");
19. 
20. use crate::hal::mem::{
21.     Address,
22.     FrameAddress,
23.     PageAligned,
24.     PhysicalAddress,
25. };
26. use ::arch::mem;
27. use ::core::ops::{
28.     Deref,
29.     DerefMut,
30. };
31. use ::sys::error::Error;
32. 
33. //==================================================================================================
34. // Kernel Frame
35. //==================================================================================================
36. 
37. /// A type that represents a kernel frame.
38. #[derive(Debug)]
39. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
40. pub struct KernelFrame {
41.     /// Frame address.
42.     base: FrameAddress,
43. }
44. 
45. // Dependency contract for the manager layer: wrapping a `FrameAddress` produces a handle whose
46. // abstract address is the same physical frame.
47. #[verus_verify]
48. impl KernelFrame {
49.     ///
50.     /// # Description
51.     ///
52.     /// Instantiates a kernel frame.
53.     ///
54.     /// # Parameters
55.     ///
56.     /// - `base`: Frame address.
57.     ///
58.     /// # Returns
59.     ///
60.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
61.     ///
62.     // Wrapping a frame produces a handle whose abstract address is the same physical frame
63.     // (`kf@ == base@`) and which is well-formed (`kf.inv()`, page alignment carried from
64.     // `base.inv()`). The identity-mapping side effect is delegated to [`KernelFrame::map_frame`],
65.     // an exec-only helper outside Verus' purview (it materializes a page-table entry through the
66.     // not-yet-verified `mm::virt` layer, whose global `identity_map_view().inv()` precondition
67.     // cannot be discharged from within `mm::phys`). Verus verifies only the pure wrap here.
68.     #[verus_spec(result =>
69.         requires
70.             base.inv(),
71.         ensures
72.             match result {
73.                 Ok(kf) => {
74.                     &&& kf@ == base@
75.                     &&& kf.inv()
76.                 },
77.                 Err(_) => true,
78.             },
79.     )]
80.     pub(super) fn new(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
81.         // Ensure the frame is identity-mapped in the kernel address space so that
82.         // Deref/DerefMut can safely access it. This lazily installs a page
83.         // table entry if needed (page tables come from a BSS pool, so no recursive frame
84.         // allocation occurs).
85.         Self::map_frame(base)?;
86. 
87.         Ok(Self { base })
88.     }
89. }
90. 
91. // Exec-only helper: installs the identity mapping for `base` via `mm::virt::identity_map_page`.
92. // VERUS REWRITE: extracted from the body of `KernelFrame::new` so the pure frame-wrap can be
93. // machine-verified while the cross-module page-table side effect is isolated behind a single,
94. // empty trusted contract (`assume_specification[ KernelFrame::map_frame ]` in kframe.spec.rs,
95. // ledgered in verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md). Inlining the side effect back into the verified
96. // `new` is impossible: (1) `identity_map_page` requires `identity_map_view().inv()`, an
97. // `uninterp spec fn` in the PRIVATE `mod identity_map` that is not re-exported and therefore
98. // cannot even be NAMED from `mm::phys`; (2) `PageAligned::from_raw_value` is external and would
99. // itself need an `assume_specification`; (3) the `error!` logging macros fail to verify
100. // ("Unsupported constant type") and would require cfg-gated exec. Option A thus multiplies
101. // trusted surface and still cannot discharge the precondition; this extraction trusts strictly
102. // less. Kept outside Verus (no `#[verus_verify]`); carries no `external_body`.
103. impl KernelFrame {
104.     fn map_frame(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
105.         let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
106.             PageAligned::from_raw_value(base.into_raw_value()).map_err(|e| {
107.                 error!("frame base is not page-aligned: {e:?}");
108.                 e
109.             })?;
110.         crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page(phys_addr).map_err(|e| {
111.             error!("failed to identity-map frame: {:?}", e);
112.             e
113.         })
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. #[verus_verify]
118. impl KernelFrame {
119. 
120.     ///
121.     /// # Description
122.     ///
123.     /// Returns the base address of the target kernel frame.
124.     ///
125.     /// # Returns
126.     ///
127.     /// The base address of the target kernel frame.
128.     ///
129.     // Pure accessor: returns the owned frame's physical address unchanged. `result@ == self@`
130.     // gives `kpage` the exact address; `result.inv()` (page alignment carried from `self.inv()`)
131.     // lets `into_page_address` and the `KernelStack` arithmetic behind it proceed.
132.     #[verus_spec(result =>
133.         requires
134.             self.inv(),
135.         ensures
136.             result@ == self@,
137.             result.inv(),
138.     )]
139.     pub fn base(&self) -> FrameAddress {
140.         self.base
141.     }
142. }
143. 
144. impl KernelFrame {
145. 
146.     ///
147.     /// # Description
148.     ///
149.     /// Clears the target kernel frame.
150.     ///
151.     /// Uses the identity-map `memset` backend so that the write runs in the kernel address space.
152.     /// This avoids a page fault when the current CR3 points to a user page directory that lacks
153.     /// the PDE for this frame's physical address.
154.     ///
155.     pub fn clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
156.         let base: *mut u8 = self.base.into_raw_value() as *mut u8;
157.         crate::mm::virt::memset(base, 0, mem::PAGE_SIZE).map_err(|e| {
158.             error!("memset failed: {:?}", e);
159.             e
160.         })
161.     }
162. }
163. 
164. /// # Safety
165. ///
166. /// `Deref` accesses the identity-mapped frame directly. The caller must ensure that the current
167. /// CR3 points to a page directory that has the relevant PDE for this frame's physical address
168. /// (i.e., the kernel page directory, or a user page directory into which the PDE has been
169. /// propagated via [`sync_kernel_pdes`](crate::mm::virt::sync_kernel_pdes)). For CR3-agnostic
170. /// writes, prefer [`KernelFrame::clear()`] which uses the identity-map `memset` backend.
171. impl Deref for KernelFrame {
172.     type Target = [u8];
173. 
174.     fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
175.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
176.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr as *const u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
177.     }
178. }
179. 
180. /// # Safety
181. ///
182. /// See [`Deref`] impl — the same CR3 invariant applies.
183. impl DerefMut for KernelFrame {
184.     fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
185.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
186.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(ptr as *mut u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
187.     }
188. }
189. 
190. #[verus_verify]
191. impl Drop for KernelFrame {
192.     // Releasing the handle returns its physical frame to the global frame allocator via
193.     // `super::frame::free`, which is best-effort (`ensures true`) and `opens_invariants none`/
194.     // `no_unwind`, so `drop` makes no abstract postcondition. Callers (the manager error path,
195.     // `KernelStack::drop`) rely on this being the sole, complete deallocation step. Mirror of
196.     // `UserFrame::drop`.
197.     #[verus_spec(
198.         opens_invariants none
199.         no_unwind
200.     )]
201.     fn drop(&mut self) {
202.         if let Err(e) = super::frame::free(self.base) {
203.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
204.             error!("failed to free kernel frame: {:?}", e);
205.         }
206.     }
207. }

1. # View Design: `mm::phys::kframe` (`KernelFrame`)
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. `KernelFrame` is an **owning handle to exactly one page-sized physical frame**.
6. To the outside world it is a single value: *which physical frame this handle
7. owns*. The only caller-observable abstract state is that frame's **physical
8. address**. Everything else — the identity-mapping side effect, how the address
9. is stored, the page-table mechanics, the byte contents reachable through
10. `Deref` — is internal or out of scope.
11. 
12. In-scope functions: `KernelFrame::new` (constructor), `KernelFrame::base`
13. (query), `KernelFrame::drop` (destructor).
14. 
15. ---
16. 
17. ## Inherited View (from upstream `mm::phys` manager verification)
18. 
19. ```rust
20. impl View for KernelFrame {
21.     type V = int;
22.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int { self.base@ }   // physical frame address
23. }
24. ```
25. 
26. This View was added when the manager layer (`alloc_kernel_frame`,
27. `alloc_many_kernel_frames`) was verified top-down. It is treated here as an
28. **input to evaluate**, not a finished design.
29. 
30. ### Evaluation against *all* callers
31. 
32. | Caller | Uses `self@` as… | Verdict |
33. |---|---|---|
34. | `manager::alloc_kernel_frame` | the allocated address: `kf@ == frame_addr@`, `lemma_kernel_alloc_one(..., result->Ok_0@)` | ✅ address |
35. | `manager::alloc_many_kernel_frames` | `kernel_frames_contiguous`, `kernel_addr_set(frames@)` — set/sequence of owned addresses | ✅ address |
36. | `virt::kpage::KernelPage::base` | `kframe.base().into_page_address().into_virtual_address()` — needs the address + page-alignment | ✅ address |
37. | `virt::kpage::KernelPage::frame_address` | returns `kframe.base()` verbatim | ✅ address |
38. | `Drop` sites (manager error path, `KernelStack::drop`) | identity of the frame being freed exactly once | ✅ address |
39. 
40. Every caller agrees: the abstract state is the **physical frame address**, an
41. `int`. No caller needs anything else.
42. 
43. **Decision: KEEP `type V = int` unchanged.** It already passes the
44. substitution test from every caller's perspective (see Rationale). Nothing is
45. renamed, added, or removed. The View definition is left exactly as inherited.
46. 
47. ---
48. 
49. ## View Struct
50. 
51. The View is a primitive, not a struct:
52. 
53. ```rust
54. impl View for KernelFrame {
55.     type V = int;                       // the physical address of the owned frame
56.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int { /* maps impl field -> address */ }
57. }
58. ```
59. 
60. - `view()` stays **`closed`**: public so callers write `kf@`, closed so the
61.   field-level mapping (currently `self.base@`) does not leak.
62. - The value space is `int` — the mathematical physical address. (Per the
63.   view-design exception, an address could keep `usize`; here the upstream View
64.   and the whole `FrameAddress`/`Inner` address algebra already work in `int`
65.   via `View::V = int`, so `int` is the consistent, cast-free choice.)
66. 
67. A wrapper struct (`KernelFrameView { addr: int }`) was considered and
68. **rejected** — see Rejected Alternatives.
69. 
70. ---
71. 
72. ## Well-formedness Invariant
73. 
74. `KernelFrame` currently has **no** `inv()`. Callers of `base()`
75. (`into_page_address`, and the page/stack address arithmetic behind it) rely on
76. the owned address being **page-aligned**. This is a caller-visible constraint
77. on the abstract state, so it belongs in `inv()`.
78. 
79. **Final decision (spec phase): single `inv()`, mirroring the verified sibling
80. `UserFrame::inv`.** The originally-sketched `internal_inv()` placeholder
81. (`pub closed spec fn internal_inv(&self) -> bool { true }`) was dropped: it would
82. be permanently `true` (the closed view `self@ == self.base@` already exposes the
83. alignment fact directly, so no implementation-consistency clause is needed), and
84. the `spec-design` skill discourages extra `pub spec fn`s on `impl MyType` beyond
85. `view`/`inv`. The result is identical in shape to `UserFrame`:
86. 
87. ```rust
88. impl KernelFrame {
89.     // Caller-visible well-formedness: the owned frame address is page-aligned.
90.     // Stated purely on the int view via the shared spec_page_size(); leaks no
91.     // implementation detail. Mirror of UserFrame::inv.
92.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
93.         self@ % spec_page_size() == 0
94.     }
95. }
96. ```
97. 
98. - `inv()` is **`pub open`** so callers can establish and consume it.
99. - `spec_page_size()` is the same `pub uninterp spec fn` already used by
100.   `FrameAddress::inv` (`self@ % spec_page_size() == 0`); reusing it keeps the
101.   alignment notion identical across the two types.
102. - No `internal_inv()` is defined; the alignment fact follows on the `new` /
103.   `base` paths directly from the required `base.inv()` / `self.inv()`.
104. 
105. No other `pub spec fn` is added to `impl KernelFrame` beyond `view` and `inv`.
106. 
107. ---
108. 
109. ## Spec Transition Functions
110. 
111. **There are none — and that is a deliberate, substitution-tested result.**
112. 
113. A `KernelFrame`'s abstract view is fixed at construction and **never changes**
114. for the lifetime of the handle. The in-scope API confirms this:
115. 
116. - `new(base)` is a **constructor**: it produces a fresh handle whose view *is*
117.   the input address. The contract is a constructor postcondition, not a
118.   transition on an existing view:
119. 
120.   ```rust
121.   // new (already external_body per tcb-allowed.md; keep its existing spec,
122.   // optionally surface the invariant it already guarantees):
123.   ensures match result {
124.       Ok(kf) => kf@ == base@ && kf.inv(),   // inv follows from required base.inv()
125.       Err(_) => true,                       // no ownership taken on failure
126.   }
127.   ```
128. 
129. - `base(&self)` is a **pure query** — no view change. Needed new spec:
130. 
131.   ```rust
132.   fn base(&self) -> (result: FrameAddress)
133.       requires self.inv(),
134.       ensures  result@ == self@ && result.inv();
135.   ```
136. 
137.   `result@ == self@` gives `kpage` the exact address; `result.inv()` (carried
138.   from `self.inv()`'s alignment clause) lets `into_page_address` and the stack
139.   arithmetic proceed.
140. 
141. - `drop(&mut self)` is a **destructor**. Its effect is *not* a transition on
142.   `KernelFrame`'s own view (the value is consumed). Dropping returns the frame
143.   `old(self)@` to the **global frame allocator**, so its postcondition is
144.   written against the allocator's View (`FrameAllocView` / `phys_view().frames`,
145.   the same View the manager already reasons over), e.g. "after drop,
146.   `old(self)@` is no longer allocated / is back in the free partition, and no
147.   other frame's status changes." Because that state lives in the allocator's
148.   abstraction, **no field is needed on `KernelFrameView` to express it**.
149. 
150. Consequently `impl KernelFrame`'s View needs no `spec_*` mutator helpers: the
151. view is immutable per handle, the only state change in the module
152. (allocation/free) is owned by the allocator's View.
153. 
154. ---
155. 
156. ## Design Rationale
157. 
158. ### Field: the view value `self@ : int` — the physical frame address
159. - **Why needed.** It is the one thing every caller reasons about: the manager
160.   proves the wrapped address equals the allocated address and builds
161.   `kernel_addr_set` / contiguity facts from it; `kpage` converts it to page and
162.   virtual addresses; `drop` frees *that* address. There is no caller use of
163.   `KernelFrame` that does not reduce to its address.
164. - **Substitution test.** *If `KernelFrame` were rewritten to store a raw
165.   `usize`, a frame number, or to compute the address on the fly instead of
166.   holding a `FrameAddress` — would "the physical frame address" still make
167.   sense?* **Yes.** Any owning-frame-handle implementation must denote *some*
168.   physical frame; its address is the implementation-independent identity of
169.   what is owned. ✅
170. - **Caller-only.** A caller understands "the physical address of the frame this
171.   handle owns" with zero knowledge of the internal field, the identity map, or
172.   page tables.
173. 
174. ### `inv()` clause: `self@ % spec_page_size() == 0` (page-aligned)
175. - **Why needed.** `base()` returns a `FrameAddress` that downstream code feeds
176.   to `into_page_address` and to `KernelStack` index arithmetic, both of which
177.   assume page alignment. Collecting this into `inv()` (instead of re-deriving it
178.   at every call site) follows the "missing wf()" anti-pattern fix.
179. - **Substitution test.** Alignment is a property of *what a physical frame is*
180.   (page-sized, page-aligned), not of how the handle stores it. Any
181.   implementation that owns a real frame yields a page-aligned address. ✅
182. - **Caller-abstract.** Stated purely on `self@` using the shared
183.   `spec_page_size()`; no implementation detail appears.
184. 
185. ### `internal_inv()` left as `true`
186. - Per methodology, implementation-consistency facts (here: "the stored
187.   `FrameAddress` satisfies its own `inv`") require seeing impl fields, so they
188.   are deferred to the spec phase. The caller-visible consequence (alignment) is
189.   already exposed through `inv()`.
190. 
191. ### Why no spec transition functions
192. - The handle's view is immutable; the only mutation in the module's lifecycle
193.   (a frame leaving the free partition on `new`'s upstream `alloc`, and returning
194.   on `drop`) is state of the **allocator**, captured by `FrameAllocView`, not by
195.   this per-object View. Modeling it here would duplicate (and risk
196.   desynchronizing) the allocator's abstraction.
197.
